findings.obs_text: In Exo 2:14 Moses, asked who made him a judge, is afraid and thinks the thing is known. In Joh 5:45 the hearers are not to think Jesus will accuse them, for Moses does. In Jam 2:4 those who make distinctions become judges with evil thoughts: the judging is done from evil thoughts.

In 1Cor 14:37 the one who thinks he is a prophet should acknowledge Paul's writing as the Lord's command: the self-view is tested by acknowledging. In Phili 3:15 where the mature think otherwise, God will reveal it to them.
findings.grounds: God will reveal that also to you

findings.obs_text: In Gen 6:5 the thoughts of the heart are evil continually: the evil is lasting. In 1Sa 27:12 Achish thinks David will always be his servant, and in Joh 5:39 the hearers think they have eternal life in the Scriptures: the thought claims a lasting state the verse shows otherwise.

In Rom 14:14 Paul is persuaded nothing is unclean in itself, yet it is unclean to the one who counts it so: the thought makes it unclean for him. In 2Cor 10:5 every thought is taken captive to obey Christ: the thought is brought to obedience.
findings.grounds: unclean for anyone who thinks it unclean

findings.obs_text: In Gen 6:5 the wickedness of man is great, and the thoughts of his heart are only evil: the wickedness seen on earth and the evil of the thoughts are named together.
findings.grounds: the wickedness of man was great in the earth

findings.obs_text: In Job 15:35 and Isa 59:4 the wicked conceive mischief and their womb prepares deceit, with lies spoken. In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are just against the deceitful counsels of the wicked. In 1Cor 3:18, Gal 6:3 and Jam 1:26 the one who thinks himself wise, something or religious deceives himself, and in 2Cor 11:3 the thoughts may be led astray by deceit as Eve was.

In 2Cor 11:3 the thoughts are to stay in sincere and pure devotion to Christ, from which deceit would lead them astray. In Heb 10:29 the hearers are asked to think of the one who profaned the blood by which he was sanctified.
findings.grounds: a sincere and pure devotion to Christ

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 20:3 David says Saul knows the favor he has with Jonathan and so thinks to keep it from him. In Pro 18:2 the fool takes no pleasure in understanding, only in airing his opinion: his delight is in his own view. In Jer 3:19 the Lord thought to give a pleasant land and be called Father.
findings.grounds: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding

older.finding: His hope for them, disappointed. *"I said, How I would set you among my sons, and give you a pleasant land … And I thought you would call me, My Father, and would not turn from following me. Surely, as a treacherous wife leaves her husband, so have you been treacherous to me"* (Jer 3:19–20).
older.reason: it states how delight works in a person; the delight collection owns it
